channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Inside Italy's Changing Politics and Papacy
item.description: New York Times Correspondent and Former Rome Bureau Chief Jason Horowitz tells Bloomberg This Weekend how his 25 years reporting from Italy gave him a firsthand view of the Vatican, papal transitions and the country's evolving political landscape. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Horowitz discusses his new memoir, The Italian Job, and how Italy's political experiments, from Silvio Berlusconi to Giorgia Meloni, offer insights into broader global trends. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India Protests Trigger Security Crackdown in New Delhi
item.description: Bloomberg Senior Reporter Dan Strumpf tells Bloomberg This Weekend that New Delhi remains under heavy security after authorities detained thousands of protesters demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a disputed revision of voter rolls. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Strumpf says the youth-led movement reflects broader frustration over unemployment and economic opportunities, with the unrest unfolding ahead of Bloomberg's New Economy Forum in the Indian capital. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Exclusive: Dimon, Farley, Gov. Whitmer on Rebuilding American Manufacturing
item.description: Ford, JPMorgan and the state of Michigan are teaming up to connect manufacturers and startups with capital, customers and government support as the US tries to rebuild supply chains that were moved overseas. Ford CEO Jim Farley says his company will commit $1 billion in purchasing to companies developing capabilities in areas including advanced manufacturing, magnets and rare earths, while JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon says the bank will lend capital through its broader security and resiliency push. Michigan’s governor Gretchen Whitmer is hopeful that the partnership will provide more opportunities for the state’s workforce. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Emerging Markets Better Armed for Renewed European Debt Turmoil
item.description: Emerging-market bonds and currencies were whipsawed by the Eurozone debt crisis 15 years ago, but they are now better equipped to withstand any repeat of that turmoil, analysts say.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Wong and Selcuk Gokoluk

item.title: Singapore F1 Race Draws Near-Record Turnout Despite Choking Haze
item.description: Singapore’s Formula 1 Grand Prix race saw a near-record turnout, bucking concerns that one of the worst regional haze in recent years would threaten the event.
item.dc:creator: Weilun Soon

item.title: Banque du Caire Offers 30% Stake in Egypt’s Second IPO in Month
item.description: Banque du Caire will sell a 30% stake via Egypt’s stock exchange, a long-awaited state-asset sale that would also be the country’s second major initial public offering in a month.
item.dc:creator: Tarek El-Tablawy

item.title: Healey Plans Short-Term UK Budget Giveaways to Limit Fiscal Pain
item.description: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey wants to help British voters with the cost of living while staying within the limits of his country’s stretched public finances. To square this circle, he’s planning a series of strictly short-term giveaways — and hoping the war in Iran comes to an end.
item.dc:creator: Joe Mayes and Philip Aldrick

item.title: Cockroach Party Leaders Vow to Continue Protests After Release
item.description: Leaders of India’s youth-led protest movement - Cockroach Janta Party - vowed to press ahead with their demand for the resignation of the country’s top election official after being released from a temporary detention on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia, Akriti Sharma and Atul Dev

item.title: China Issues Draft Standards for Remanufactured Automotive Parts
item.description: China released draft rules that would establish nationwide requirements for automotive-parts remanufacturing, including standards for the sourcing of used components, product quality, traceability and market oversight.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: India’s Rupee Defense Raises Question of How Far RBI Will Go
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India is broadening its defenses to steady the rupee, taking some of its strongest measures since the 2013 taper tantrum. That may give the currency a boost as trading resumes Monday, but the question remains: how far is the central bank willing to go as external pressures mount?
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Sircar and Bhaskar Dutta

item.title: Once-Hot AI Trade Leaves Korean Stocks Struggling for Buyers
item.description: South Korea spent much of this year as a poster child of the scorching global AI trade. Now, by almost every measure, the $4.3 trillion stock market is rapidly losing relevance with investors.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Yang, Winnie Hsu and Abhishek Vishnoi

item.title: AI Debt Issuance Defies Rising Yields as SpaceX, Broadcom Plan Major Deals
item.description: When financing gets more expensive, companies usually slow down their bond sales. Tech companies have instead been ramping up this year, and talk this week of potential big financings from SpaceX and Broadcom Inc. only amplified investor fears about the wave of coming debt.
item.dc:creator: Tasos Vossos

item.title: Strong Earnings Keep US Stocks in Favor
item.description: PNC Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati tells Bloomberg This Weekend that strong corporate fundamentals and resilient consumer spending could support US stocks as investors head into third-quarter earnings season. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Agati says investors will be watching for evidence that AI investment is generating returns beyond the largest technology companies, while strong US earnings growth keeps her favoring domestic equities over developed international markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Viral Handbags Turn Small Designer Into Fashion Star
item.description: New York Handbag Designer Pierre Laborde tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a viral TikTok video transformed his handmade leather bags from a longtime fixture at a local street market into a sought-after fashion accessory, with demand now exceeding his small team's production capacity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Laborde says he plans to preserve the individuality and craftsmanship of his designs rather than pursue mass production or partnerships with major retailers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: The growing debate over video calls on airplanes, premium California wines selling at steep discounts under supermarket private labels, a new rivalry between New York diners featuring singing waiters and the growing popularity of elaborate tuna carving experiences at high-end sushi restaurants. Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hurricane Isaias May Cost Insurers Billions
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Insurance Equity Analyst Matthew Palazola tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Hurricane Isaias could generate insured losses in the single-digit billions of dollars, with stronger Florida building codes potentially limiting damage despite rising property values. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Palazola says two relatively mild hurricane seasons have helped insurers rebuild capital, while recent Florida insurance reforms have improved market conditions but have yet to face a major test. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jefferies Says Found Fraud in $900 Million of Radiant Deals
item.description: A Jefferies-run fund said in court proceedings that it has evidence of alleged fraudulent conduct by iron ore traders Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals in receivables-financing deals with a face value of almost $900 million.
item.dc:creator: Upmanyu Trivedi, Jack Farchy and Archie Hunter

item.title: Taiwan’s Lai Urges Democracies to Unite After Trump-Xi Talks
item.description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te called on democracies in the region to unite against threats to stability, as the island faces pressure from Beijing and concerns that US President Donald Trump’s rapprochement with China could come at Taiwan’s expense.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: Phenomenal Time To Be Investor, Not Consumer: Amoroso
item.description: Anastasia Amoroso, chief investment strategist with Partners Group, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the bullish sentiment in the stock market, the potential for volatility in the near future, and rising global yields. (Source: Bloomberg)
